newsitem.title: UK: ISMA says continues to work on EMU implications.
newsitem.headline: ISMA says continues to work on EMU implications.

text.p: The International Securities Market Association (ISMA) has created a small working party to study the implications and ramifications of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), it said in its 1996 annual report on Tuesday.
ISMA said it was close to issuing a number of formal recommendations to the membership at large.
ISMA said it was also involved in "The Forum", an initiative born of a desire to monitor the practical implications of EMU on the international securities market as a whole.

It said The Forum had published a set of basic recommendations aimed at making the conversion to the euro as simple, smooth and cost effective as possible for both the financial industry and the investor community as a whole.

The European Capital Markets Institute, of which ISMA is a founder member, has also commissioned a major reserch project from INSEAD on the implications and ramifications of EMU on European capital markets which will be available early in 1998.
ISMA said it remained strictly neutral as to the potential benefits of EMU.
